subject: Request: Canary / A-B traffic-shift policy as SLA exception
messages:
From: Julie Han <julie.han@acme.io>
To: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acme.io
Date: 2026-04-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Requesting SLA exception for canary traffic-shift during rollout

Hi Aditya,

We're preparing for a phased rollout of Redwood-powered features across our customer-facing product and procurement needs to sign off on the SLA language. Our security and ops teams want a documented exception that permits a controlled canary / A-B traffic-shift for up to 72 hours when deploying new model versions, with clear automatic fallback behavior to protect our SLOs.

High-level asks: 
- A short description of your canary traffic-shift policy (ramp schedule, health checks).
- What automatic fallback triggers you support (error rates, latency thresholds, regen failures).
- Pinning options: can we pin an application to a specific model runtime/version?
- A one-page term we can attach to the contract that creates a temporary SLA exception during the canary window.

I've attached a brief request doc (Acme-SLA-request.pdf) with procurement's timeline — they need a proposed term by EOD Thursday.

Thanks,
Julie Han
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme Cloud Solutions

From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Julie Han <julie.han@acme.io>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-11T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Requesting SLA exception for canary traffic-shift during rollout

Julie — thanks for the clear ask and the doc. We're happy to support a controlled canary window with automatic safeguards. Quick proposal and next steps below: 

Summary (short): Redwood can support a temporary SLA exception for a canary period (up to 72 hours) where a traffic-shift A-B deployment is used. During the canary we will: 
- Ramp traffic according to a predefined schedule (e.g., 5% -> 25% -> 50% over configurable intervals).
- Apply health checks and automated fallback to the previous pinned version if thresholds are exceeded.
- Allow customers to pin to a specific model version/runtime at the route level.

To finalize for procurement we need to confirm: 
1) The exact fallback triggers you want (we often use p95 latency and 5xx rate but can adjust).
2) The max traffic and ramp cadence.
3) Whether Redwood should initiate an automatic rollback or only notify your on-call before rolling back.

I've looped in our infra lead, Marcus Lin, and our legal/commercial lead, Laura Bennett, to prepare a one-page term and a short technical annex. Marcus — could you put together a 2-3 bullet technical summary we can share with Acme that lists default thresholds, pin behavior, and a quick note on how we implement fallback?

I'll prep a draft term and attach a proposed canary policy PDF for procurement.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>

Marcus / Laura — forwarding Julie's request from Acme. Procurement needs a short technical summary for the procurement term-sheet (EOD Thu). Key points they want covered: ramp schedule examples, automatic fallback triggers, pinning/versioning semantics, and whether fallback is automatic or manual by default. 

Please keep it short (3–5 bullets) so I can paste into the term-sheet. Also flag any operational caveats (e.g., KV cache invalidation after rollback) we should call out.

Thanks — Aditya

From: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-11T13:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Requesting SLA exception for canary traffic-shift during rollout — need brief technical summary

Aditya / Laura — see bullets below; keeping this concise for procurement. Feel free to edit language when sharing with Acme.

Technical summary (can paste into the term-sheet):
- Canary traffic-shift: Redwood supports staged traffic ramps by percentage (example default: 5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%). Each step duration is configurable (recommended default: 15–30 minutes per step).
- Health checks & fallback triggers: automatic fallback will be triggered if any of the following occur during the canary window: sustained 5xx error rate > 1% for 5 minutes, p95 latency increase > 40% relative to baseline, or repeated token-generation failures (>= 3 per minute).
- Rollback behavior: on fallback we automatically route inbound traffic back to the pinned/previous model version and flush only ephemeral per-request caches; KV/prefix caches are preserved where possible to minimize cold-start regressions.
- Pinning: customers can pin a route to a specific model version/runtime (e.g., model-v1.12-quant) via the API or Console; pinned versions are exempt from automatic replacement during rollouts.
- Control mode: default is automatic fallback + alerting to both Redwood and customer on-call. We can offer manual-only rollback on request (requires ops approval and will extend canary duration).

Operational caveats:
- If the canary model uses a different quantization profile, there may be a transient increase in p95 latency during the first 10–20 min of traffic; we include a short warmup step to mitigate this.
- For strict SLAs, recommend enabling our prefix/KV caching to reduce sensitivity to small latency spikes.

Related runbook and policy (internal): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcDeFG_canary-policy

Marcus Lin
Staff Engineer, Inference Platform | Redwood Inference

From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Julie Han <julie.han@acme.io>, procurement@acme.io
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-12T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed term + technical annex for canary window (SLA exception)

Julie — thanks for the patience. Attached are two docs: a one-page term-sheet (SLA-exception-term-sheet.pdf) that procurement can attach to the contract, and a short proposed-canary-policy.pdf that describes the operational defaults. Summary below for quick review: 

Proposed one-line term (draft): 
During a confirmed canary deployment window not to exceed 72 hours, Redwood may temporarily suspend strict uptime/latency SLA enforcement for the affected route(s) while conducting staged traffic-shift testing, provided that Redwood maintains automatic fallback safeguards and notification procedures as described in the attached technical annex.

Key operational defaults we propose: 
- Ramp schedule: 5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%, 20-minute step default (customer can shorten/lengthen).
- Fallback triggers (automatic): sustained 5xx > 1% over 5 minutes, p95 latency > 40% over baseline, or >=3 token-generation faults/minute.
- Pinning: customers may pin to a specific model version; pinned routes will not be rolled forward during the canary.
- Control preference: default = automatic fallback + alerting; optional = manual rollback only (written request).

Next steps: 
1) Please confirm whether the fallback triggers above are acceptable for Acme (or provide target thresholds).
2) If acceptable, procurement/Legal can attach the one-page term and we will include the technical annex as an exhibit.
3) If Acme prefers manual-only rollback, note that in the term and we will generate a short Ops playbook for the run.

Attachments: proposed-canary-policy.pdf, SLA-exception-term-sheet.pdf

Regards,
Aditya Rao
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Julie Han <julie.han@acme.io>
To: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Proposed term + technical annex for canary window (SLA exception)

Aditya / Team — this looks good and aligns with what our SREs expected. Two small asks before procurement attaches the term: 
1) Reduce the p95 threshold to 30% (from 40%) — our baseline is tight.
2) Add a 10-minute warmup step at the very start of the canary at 1% traffic to pre-warm caches.

If you can accept those, procurement will attach the one-page term and sign the DocuSign. We'll finish signatures by Friday. Thanks for the quick turnaround.

Best,
Julie Han
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme Cloud Solutions
